crile-kelly-kocher-and-allis-clamps.title: Common clamps by name
crile-kelly-kocher-and-allis-clamps.caption: A picture guide to common clamps by name: Crile hemostat: Atraumatic, non-toothed. Grasps vessels that will be tied off; Kelly clamp: Larger hemostat for grasping larger tissues or vessels.
crile-kelly-kocher-and-allis-clamps.body:
In short: A picture guide to common clamps by name: Crile hemostat: Atraumatic, non-toothed. Grasps vessels that will be tied off; Kelly clamp: Larger hemostat for grasping larger tissues or vessels.

Common clamps by name

  • Crile hemostat: Atraumatic, non-toothed. Grasps vessels that will be tied off
  • Kelly clamp: Larger hemostat for grasping larger tissues or vessels
  • Kocher clamp: Traumatic, toothed. Holds tissue that will be removed
  • Allis and Babcock: Slightly rounded jaws. Both are used to grasp intestine

Why it matters in theatre

Instruments and equipment are the working tools of surgery. Recognising each one by name and purpose lets you prepare and pass the right one quickly and care for it properly.

Remember

Locking clamps can be traumatic or atraumatic. Check the jaws.

Check yourself

Name the items shown on "Common clamps by name".

Crile hemostat: Atraumatic, non-toothed. Grasps vessels that will be tied off; Kelly clamp: Larger hemostat for grasping larger tissues or vessels; Kocher clamp: Traumatic, toothed. Holds tissue that will be removed; Allis and Babcock: Slightly rounded jaws. Both are used to grasp intestine.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

Sources: ACS Division of Education, Common Surgical Instruments module.
